articles.text: ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Xiǎo Míngzi, jīntian zěnme yǒu shíjiān zài jiā?
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Xiǎo Míngzi, how is it that you have time to be at home today?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Zěnme méi shíjiān? Líkāi xuéxiào yǐhòu, shíjiān duōduō le.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: How would I not have time? Since I left school, I've had lots more time.
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Bié húshuō. Nǐ yǒu gōngzuò le meiyou?
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Cut it out. Do you have a job yet?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Yǒu gōngzuò! Yǒule gōngzuò hái zài zhèr zuòzhe! Nǐ zhēn yǒu yìsi!
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Have a job! If I had a job would I still be sitting here! You're something else!
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Ou! Wǒ zhīdao le, nǐ hái méi gōngzuò na!
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Oh! I see, you still don't have a job!
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Ng. Lǎoshī shuō wǒ kěyi děngyiděng.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Uh-huh. My teachers said I can wait a while.
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Nǐ zhèiyang děngxiaqu zěnme xíng ne? Yìtian méi gōngzuò, yìtian jiù děi kào fùmǔ a.
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: How will it do for you to go on waiting like this? Every day you don't have a job, you have to depend on your parents.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Hài, wǒ yě zhīdao, zhèiyang xiaqu bù xíng, kěshi wǒ shízài xiǎngbuchū shénme hǎo bànfǎ ya! Nǐ shuō wǒ zěnme bàn?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: (Sigh) I know that it won't do to go on like this, but I really can't think of any good solution! What do you think I should do?
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Nǐ huì shénme?
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: What do you know how to do?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Wǒ shénme dōu bú huì. Xiàng Xiǎo Lín tāmen huì zuò zhuōzi yǐzi shénmede, yě dōu yǒu gōngzuò le.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: I don't know how to do anything. Like Xiǎo Lín and the others, who can make tables, chairs, and so on — they all have jobs already.
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Ēi, nǐ huì bu huì zhào xiàng?
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Say, can you take photographs?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Bú huì.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: No.
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Nǐ duì zhào xiàng yǒu méiyou xìngqù?
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Are you interested in photography?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Yǒu a!
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Sure!
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Zhèiyàng ba! Wǒ yǒu yíge Rìběn zhàoxiàngjī, wǒ jiāo ni zěnmeyàng zhào xiàng, nǐ jiù kěyi yǒu gōngzuò le.
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: How about this: I have a Japanese camera. I'll teach you how to take pictures, and then you can have a job.
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Suàn le ba, huì zhào xiàng zěnme huì yǒu gōngzuò ne!
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Come on! How can I have a job by knowing how to take pictures!

ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Hài, nǐ zhēn bù cōngming. Měitian dōu yǒu bù shǎo rén lái Běijīng, shéi bù xiǎng zài Tiān'ānmén qián zhào zhāng xiàng! Nǐ zài zhǎo liǎngge tóngxué, yǒu guǎn zhàoxiàngde, yǒu guǎn shōu qiánde, bú jiù xíng le ma?

MIDDLE-AGED MAN: Tsk, you're really not on the ball. Every day there are lots of people who come to Běijīng; who doesn't want to get their picture taken in front of Tiān'ānmén! If you find a couple of classmates, and have one in charge of taking the pictures and one in charge of collecting the money, then you're all set, right?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: Nín shuōde yǒu dàolǐ, jiù zhème bàn! Duì le, yào chūqu zhào xiàng, hái xūyào shēnqǐng ba?
XIǍO MÍNGZI: What you say makes sense; that's just what I'll do! Oh yes — if you want to go out and take pictures, you have to apply, too, don't you?
ZHŌNGNIÁN RÉN: Nà róngyi. Míngtian, nǐ qù zhǎo lǎoshī, tāmen huì bāngzhu nǐ bànde.
MIDDLE-AGED MAN: That's easy. Tomorrow, go see your teachers. They'll help you do it.
